question.text: A ULIP policyholder wants to surrender the policy after 3 years of investment. What is the regulatory position on this?

answer.text: The policyholder can surrender/discontinue after 3 years, but payout is deferred until the 5-year lock-in ends, after a capped discontinuation charge (up to Rs. 6,000) and transfer of the balance to the discontinuation policy fund
The policyholder can surrender at any time and will receive the full fund value minus a 2% exit load
The policyholder can surrender after 3 years with a minimum guaranteed surrender value of 30% of premiums paid
The policyholder must wait for the full policy term to complete before any withdrawal is permitted

explanation.text: The Logic: ULIPs have a 5-year lock-in. Surrender or discontinuation before the end of the lock-in is permitted, but a discontinuation charge capped at Rs. 6,000 is deducted and the balance is transferred to a discontinuation policy fund. The surrender value is paid out only at the end of the 5-year lock-in period. The Trap: The 30% minimum surrender value rule applies to traditional policies, not ULIPs. There is no "2% exit load" — the charge is capped at Rs. 6,000. The funds are not locked until the full policy term; only until the 5-year lock-in ends. Note: The Rs. 6,000 cap is the maximum discontinuation charge — actual charges vary by year of discontinuation and are typically lower in later years. Always review the policy document for the specific discontinuation charge schedule.
